newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu says "terrorism" ends peace process.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says "terrorism" ends peace process.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that Arab-Israeli peace talks have come to a halt because of "terrorism" that Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat could stop.

"I think we have had here a virtual collapse of the peace process," Netanyahu said on CBS television's "Face the Nation" programme. "What we have found here, though, is that the Palestinian side has unleashed terrorism as a weapon of negotiation. We want to see the peace process continue without the threat of terrorism."
Asked if he felt Arafat was in control, Netanyahu replied: "I think he is able to control and quell all violence."
He added: "We are not sure at this point that all the terrorists have been curbed. They should jail them ... make sure that they cannot act."

Netanyahu said he doubted Arab nations would cut ties to Israel because of continuing street battles between Israeli soldiers and Palestinians demonstrating against Israel's decision to start building new homes for Jews in historically Arab East Jerusalem.

"I would urge the Arab countries to think of their larger interests, their longer interests, as I urge the Palestinians for the necessity of peace," he said. "I don't think they would do it, and if they did it would cost them as much as it costs us," he added about speculation that Arab governments would rebuke Israel by severing relations.

Sunday was the 11th day of unrest sparked by Israel's breaking ground for the new Jewish homes. Israel has demanded a crackdown on the demonstrations by the Palestinian Authority headed by Arafat, who pledged to do his best to curb violence.

The killing of a Palestinian by Israeli troops on Saturday raised tensions for Land Day, an annual day of protests by Arabs. Some 850,000 Arabs live in the Jewish state, and the community annually commemorates the killing by Israeli forces of six Arabs during land demonstrations in 1976.

At an Arab foreign ministers meeting in Cairo, Arafat urged them to press on with plans for a special "uniting for peace" U.N. General Assembly session to bypass U.S. vetoes of Security Council resolutions critical of Israel.
He said Israel had declared war on the Palestinian people by surrounding Palestinian areas with tanks in response to protesting Palestinians throwing stones.
